question_text: What key specs do you look at when selecting an N-channel power MOSFET as a low-side switch?
answer_text:
1. Drain-Source Breakdown (V_ds): Max voltage when off.
2. V_gs Threshold: Gate voltage where it starts turning on (Verify it reaches full saturation at logic levels!).
3. R_ds_on: On-state resistance (keep low to stop heating).
4. Gate Charge (Q_g): Charge needed to switch states.
5. Max Continuous Current (I_d).
explanation_text: Don't just look at the V_gs threshold! A MOSFET might turn on at 2V, but requires 5V on the gate to fully saturate. Driving it with 3.3V will leave it in the ohmic region, causing it to overheat.
bonus_question_text: What dictates the max power a MOSFET package can dissipate?
bonus_answer_text: The Max Junction Temperature limit combined with its Junction-to-Ambient thermal resistance (θ_JA).
